label: early original-phase input of b (also s, z, k, j), first of that group
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (98% of mass), at early positions t=1..3 (t=2 alone holds 54% of mass; never at t=0, the delimiter, or later original steps). The input token sets the magnitude: b is strongest (42% of mass, 11x lift), then s, z, k, j, with weaker p, a, g. It fires mostly on the first occurrence of the token. Magnitude also goes up when the preceding prefix contains h, x, c, 2, 0, w or e (the top examples look like x h c [b]). It is near-silent in the copy phase. Precision is low: the same tokens at the same positions often stay below threshold when the prefix context is unfavorable, which suggests it is a graded sum of token-and-context evidence rather than a clean boolean. Dev F1 is about 0.35 and mass recall 0.77. Adding a first-token context condition only raised F1 to 0.37.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: b, s; t=2: b, s, z, k; t=4: b, s, z, k) and the first original token (most: h, x, c, 2, 0, d; least: p, z, a, b); timing cues that raise it most: t=2, t=3, L=4 & t=6.
